children: According to ChainCatcher, Fluidkey said attackers exploited two vulnerabilities in SigNoz, its self-hosted logging tool, to read internal logs and obtain user session tokens, stealing about $1.6 million from 52 accounts. The attackers used the tokens to create and approve transfer requests, raise two-factor authentication payment limits, and trigger notifications with small transfers. After users opened and unlocked the app, it signed unauthorized transfers prepared in advance. The private keys controlling funds never left users’ devices.

Attackers also accessed partial profile information for 70 accounts and viewing keys for 54 newly registered accounts. The keys could reveal addresses, balances, and transaction histories, but could not transfer funds. Fluidkey said it updated the logging tool, ended existing login sessions, and strengthened transfer authorization checks. Service resumed on November 20 at 11:27 PM (UTC+8). The company is tracking the stolen funds with blockchain investigation firm zeroShadow.

title: Fluidkey Says SigNoz Log Flaws Exposed Session Tokens in $1.6M Theft
